title: Data Leakage
description: The parent user may unintentionally share sensitive information (email, password, name, govt ID) during registration, leading to potential data leakage if the information is intercepted or misused.

title: Insecure Data Storage
description: The authentication service may store sensitive user data (email, password, name, govt ID) insecurely, making it vulnerable to unauthorized access or breaches.

title: Data Misuse
description: The authentication service may misuse the collected data (email, password, name, govt ID) for purposes other than intended, such as marketing or profiling without user consent.

title: Unintended Disclosure
description: There is a risk that the authentication service may unintentionally disclose sensitive user information to unauthorized parties due to misconfigurations or vulnerabilities.

title: Data Disclosure from Authentication Service
description: The authentication service may unintentionally disclose personal data when storing parent account information in the MongoDB users collection, especially if the data includes sensitive information that is not strictly necessary for the operation.

title: Data Disclosure in MongoDB
description: The MongoDB users collection may expose personal data to unauthorized access or breaches, leading to potential data disclosure of parent account information stored within it.

title: Data Leakage
description: The authentication service may inadvertently expose sensitive user data (e.g., JWT tokens) to unauthorized parties during the transmission process.

title: Insecure Data Handling
description: The parent user may mishandle the received JWT and user data, leading to potential exposure or misuse of sensitive information.

title: Data Misuse
description: The parent user may use the received data in ways that violate user privacy, such as sharing it with third parties without consent.

title: Legitimate User Data Exposure
description: The child user may inadvertently expose their parent’s email and password during the login process, especially if the device is shared or compromised.

title: Insecure Data Storage
description: The authentication service may store the parent’s email and password insecurely, making it vulnerable to unauthorized access.

title: Data Misuse by Service Provider
description: The authentication service may misuse the parent’s email and password for purposes other than authentication, such as marketing or profiling.

title: Legitimate Access Threat
description: The Authentication Service (Process) may inadvertently share JWTs with unauthorized Child Users, leading to unauthorized access to child profiles.

title: Insecure Data Handling
description: The Child User (External Entity) may mishandle the received JWT and child profiles, leading to potential exposure of sensitive information.

title: Data Retention Risk
description: The Child User (External Entity) may retain the JWT and child profiles longer than necessary, increasing the risk of unauthorized access or data breaches.

title: Linking of Child Data
description: The act of sharing child profile data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) by the parent may lead to linking threats, where the combination of these attributes could be used to identify the child or associate them with other data, leading to privacy implications.

title: Inadequate Information Control
description: Once the child profile data is received by the Child Profile Management process, there is a risk that the data may be inadequately controlled, leading to unauthorized access or misuse of sensitive information.

title: Data Disclosure Risk
description: The processing of sensitive child profile data may lead to unintentional data disclosure, especially if the data is not properly secured or if access controls are insufficient.

title: Data Disclosure from Child Profile Management
description: The process of storing or updating child profiles may lead to the unintended disclosure of personal data, either through explicit sharing or implicit leakage via metadata or derived data.

title: Data Disclosure in MongoDB Child Profiles Collection
description: The MongoDB child profiles collection may inadvertently disclose personal data if proper access controls and data minimization principles are not enforced, leading to potential exposure of sensitive information.

title: Lack of User Consent
description: The Child User may not have provided explicit consent for their data to be used in video searches, requests, likes, or comments, leading to a lack of lawful basis for processing personal data.

title: Improper Personal Data Management
description: The Video Management Service may not manage personal data properly, leading to potential non-compliance with data protection regulations, such as failing to delete data when no longer necessary or not ensuring data accuracy.

title: Identified Information in Metadata
description: The metadata associated with video files may contain identifiable information, which could lead to the identification of individuals if accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Data Disclosure of Personal Data
description: The storage and retrieval of video metadata and files may inadvertently lead to the disclosure of personal data, either through explicit sharing or implicit exposure via metadata.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The process of storing child search and watch history may lead to the unintended disclosure of personal data if proper access controls are not implemented. This could result in sensitive information being exposed to unauthorized parties.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Once the child profiles are stored in the MongoDB collection, there is a risk of data disclosure if the database is not adequately secured, allowing unauthorized access to personal data.

title: Lack of User Consent
description: The parent user may upload videos without providing explicit consent for the processing of their personal data, leading to a lack of legal basis for data processing.

title: Improper Personal Data Management
description: The Video Management Service may not manage personal data properly, leading to potential non-compliance with data protection regulations.

title: Lack of consent for data sharing
description: The video management service may stream videos to the child user without obtaining proper consent, leading to a lack of legal compliance and potential privacy violations.

title: Improper personal data management
description: The child user may not manage their personal data properly after receiving the video, leading to potential misuse or exposure of sensitive information.

title: Data Disclosure from Child Profiles
description: The child browsing data being shared from the MongoDB childprofiles collection may lead to the disclosure of personal data, either explicitly or implicitly, to the AI Recommendation Engine. This could include sensitive information about children's online behavior and preferences.

title: Data Disclosure by AI Recommendation Engine
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may process and store the child browsing data in a way that leads to unintended data disclosures, either through data retention policies or by generating insights that could be shared with third parties.

title: Data Disclosure to Third-Party Advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (Process P4) shares browsing data with third-party advertisers (External Entity EE3), which may include personal data of users, leading to potential data disclosure risks.

title: Data Disclosure by Third-Party Advertisers
description: Once the browsing data is received by third-party advertisers (External Entity EE3), there is a risk that they may misuse or improperly disclose the personal data, leading to privacy violations.

title: Data Disclosure of Government ID Images
description: The authentication service (Process) may unintentionally disclose government ID images during the storage process, either through explicit sharing with unauthorized parties or through implicit means such as metadata exposure.

title: Data Disclosure of Stored Government ID Images
description: The file system (DataStore) may expose stored government ID images to unauthorized access or breaches, leading to potential data disclosure of sensitive personal information.

title: Linkability Threat
description: The act of storing JWT in localStorage can lead to linkability threats if the JWT contains identifiable information that can be linked to a user’s actions across different sessions or applications.

title: Inaccessibility Threat
description: If the JWT stored in localStorage is not properly secured, it may be accessible to unauthorized scripts or browser extensions, leading to potential information leakage.

title: Data Disclosure Threat
description: The JWT stored in localStorage may be exposed to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks, allowing attackers to retrieve sensitive information from the token.

title: Linking of Child Data to Parent
description: The process of retrieving child history for parent review may lead to linking the child's data with the parent's identity, potentially exposing sensitive information about the child.

title: Inadequate Identity Verification
description: The parent user may not be adequately verified before accessing the child's profile, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive information.
